content.text: In the last lesson, we explored object pronouns and how they function in sentences to replace nouns receiving the action. We learned to distinguish between subject and object pronouns and practiced using them naturally in real-life contexts.
Rewrite the sentence using the correct object pronoun:
“I saw Mary and John yesterday. I talked to Mary and John.” → “I talked to ___.”
refers to the way words change form to match each other in number, person, gender, or tense. This ensures that sentences are grammatically correct and clear.
Agreement can occur in several forms:
: The subject and verb must match in number and person.
: A pronoun must match its antecedent in number and gender.
“Every student must bring his or her book.”
Agreement is crucial for coherence. Mistakes often confuse listeners/readers or create ambiguity. At C1 level, mastering agreement means navigating complex structures without errors.

b) Neither the cat nor the dogs ___ (likes / like) the new food.
Each of the girls took ___ (her / their) turn.
Nobody ___ (was / were) late for the meeting.

a) “Each of them are ready.” / “Each of them is ready.”
